bugs.summary: format() wrong for subnormal numbers with double-precision powl() (musl aarch64)
bugs.creator: jeroenooms

comments.text:
Created attachment 4052
Patch case where kp <= R_dec_min_exponent

On aarch64 with musl libc (Alpine Linux), subnormal numbers are printed
incorrectly:

  > print(1.2e-313)
  [1] 1.200000e-313                     # expected 1.2e-313
  > as.character(c(1.2e-313, 1.4e-313))
  [1] "1e-313" "1e-313"

This makes `tests/reg-tests-1d.R` fail ("very small ranges" pretty() check:
`rEd <= ... are not all TRUE)`, because distinct values format identically.

Cause: scientific() in `src/main/format.c` computes `powl(10.0, kp)`, with `kp`
down to about -338 for subnormal x. On aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad,
and musl's `powl()` for 113-bit long double is a stub that calls the double
pow() (musl `src/math/powl.c`: "TODO: broken implementation to make things
compile"). So 10^kp loses precision below DBL_MIN, or underflows to 0:
`powl(10, -319) = 9.99988867e-320`, `powl(10, -327) = 0`.

Fix (attached): when `kp <= R_dec_min_exponent`, compute 10^kp as the
product of two powl() calls with normal-range exponents. The product is
formed in long double, so it does not underflow. This only affects x
below ~1e-293. On platforms with a correct powl() the result is
unchanged: on Debian aarch64 (glibc), output of print()/format()/
as.character() was byte-identical before and after the patch, for edge
cases and for 1e5 random subnormals. With the patch, R-devel on Alpine
aarch64 passes make check-all.


Check log *before* the patch: https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/actions/runs/43283038054/job/131409079104
Check log *after* the patch: https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/actions/runs/43354397036/job/131652819091
